To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
'New Governance' is a new funding model for Danish hospitals that is based on Activity Based Funding but also on a broader understanding of governance and the role of hospitals in society.
'New Governance' successfully challenged Activity Based Funding through a mix of discursive mechanisms.
'New Governance' successfully challenged the dominance of Activity Based Funding by using a mix of governance logic and by carefully engineering the model in a specific discursive context.
In summary, our research is concerned with

how the international/national discourse of Activity Based funding was successfully challenged and how this contributed to the development of a new model of hospital funding and hospital governance in Denmark.
how policy ideas are translated into concrete policy initiatives and how they are then defended and legitimized.
the question of how to create and implement new governance models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the discursive mechanisms that were used in Denmark to create 'New Governance' are not universal, but that they may be useful in other countries as well.
'New Governance' is a promising alternative to Activity Based Funding.
the discursive approach is a fruitful tool in understanding the development of alternative funding and governance models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Activity Based Funding is not an all or nothing model and that the discursive mechanisms identified can be used to challenge and change the model in a way which is more acceptable to the local actors.
the success of the Danish experiment in challenging Activity Based Funding is based on a careful and deliberate discursive engineering.
the discursive mechanisms identified in this study could be useful tools for policy makers who want to challenge Activity Based Funding.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the development of alternative models to Activity Based Funding needs to be carefully engineered.
it is possible to move away from Activity Based Funding and that there is a need for further research to develop new models.
there is a need to understand how alternative governance models are created and how they relate to Activity Based Funding.
